limitations: One matching repeat does not establish general repeatability, variance, identical trajectories or identical timing.
Sampled acceptance does not establish a continuous-time guarantee, realtime, superiority or a unique physical cause.
view.binding_resolution: Each executions row supplies execution/structure/scientific identities; facts[metric] selects the immutable fact ID and canonical value/unit. metric_sources resolve original sources. Full expanded ledger retained in archive.

scientific_question.frozen_pre_experiment_question: Can design and control adaptation improve joint reach-and-hold robustness under predefined small initial-state variation around an already successful configuration?
scientific_question.current_question: Choose the next legal decision from updated bound feedback, including recorded matching repeats.

terminal.definition: Euclidean world tip position error at the final execution sample; sealed evaluate.reach is the outcome authority.

duration.definition: Final closed interval [task duration - window, task duration].

position.definition: Maximum sampled world tip position error in the final interval.

speed.definition: Maximum sampled world tip translational speed norm in the final interval.

coverage.definition: Both endpoints, timestamps aligned to task sample_period_s; missing samples are unavailable, never a pass.

speed.definition: Euclidean norm of tip-site translational Jacobian times recorded backend qvel, reconstructed with sealed robot.xml and qpos; no finite differencing

control_period.definition: Simulated control spacing; synchronous wall overruns do not imply skipped applied updates or injected actuator delay.

duration.definition: Simulated task horizon, separate from computation wall time.

timing.interpretation: Applied updates, initialization selections, simulated duration and measured wall time are separate facts.

policy.rule: Joint acceptance first; otherwise componentwise physical comparison.
policy.tradeoff: Any physical improvement accompanied by physical worsening is a trade-off, not overall improvement.
policy.computation: Reported separately; never substitutes for reach or holding acceptance.
policy.objective: Raw scalar objectives under different weights are not ranked.

chronology.authority: Original reservation/completion events; current roles retained above

working_context.observations_scope: Observed bound facts; frozen_pre_experiment_background is historical.
working_context.repeatability_scope: No explicit matching repeat in this supplied scope; other scopes are not ruled out.

hypotheses.statement: The incumbent nominal configuration satisfies joint reach-and-hold acceptance with holding-speed margin 0.007249744484051584 m/s (0.012750255515948416 vs 0.02) and position/terminal margins below 0.01 m.
hypotheses.uncertainty: Deterministic single sampled run; margins are not robustness, repeatability or continuous-time guarantees.

hypotheses.scope: exposed subsequent near_z_plus event, candidate shared-path-v11-near-section-096 (near section scale 0.96)
hypotheses.statement: Holding-window tip speed is the fragile acceptance component under the specified small initial-state perturbation family; the exposed event exceeded only the 0.02 m/s holding-speed limit while terminal and holding position passed.
hypotheses.uncertainty: Different candidate and different case than the incumbent; not a matched nominal reference, so it motivates but does not evidence incumbent robustness.

hypotheses.scope: hypothesis for the proposed control_search batch
hypotheses.statement: Raising the holding tip-speed penalty is a plausible control lever to lower in-window tip speed, but any perturbation-robustness value is unmeasurable because only the zero-perturbation nominal case is executable.
hypotheses.uncertainty: No matched perturbation executions available; nominal initial perturbation is exactly zero.

unresolved_questions: Incumbent robustness to the four frozen perturbation cases is untested and not executable in this pilot.
Whether a stronger holding penalty reduces holding speed monotonically and without a position trade-off is unknown.
The near_z_plus event involves a different candidate identity, so it cannot be compared to the incumbent.
No repeatability or variance evidence exists for any configuration.
